subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What are the main types of concerns patients come in with in these visit notes?

judge.implied_focus: The clinical type/category of the patient's presenting concern (chief complaint) in each visit note

per_column.name: concern_category
per_column.rationale: Directly operationalises the focus by classifying each visit's presenting concern into a coherent taxonomy of clinical concern types (Musculoskeletal, Cardiovascular, Mental Health, etc.), which is exactly the decomposition the query asks for.

per_column.name: chief_complaint
per_column.rationale: Extracts the specific presenting concern as free text, providing the granular basis from which the category is inferred. It is a coherent facet of the same focus, though highly granular and mostly unique rather than an analytical grouping.

judge.rationale: Both added columns centre tightly on one coherent, data-inferable focus: the type of concern a patient presents with, which is precisely what the query targets. concern_category supplies a clean, useful-granularity categorical decomposition that directly answers 'main types of concerns.' chief_complaint adds the raw extracted concern, coherent with the focus but nearly one-value-per-row, so it functions more as source detail than as a distinct analytical facet, slightly weakening the structural differentiation (it is close to a restatement feeding the category). Still, the pair forms a sound extract-then-categorise structure. The implied focus is clearly actionable: an analyst can rank concern categories, cross-tabulate with department/urgency/age_group, and investigate high-frequency clusters. Structure_quality is held below the top because the second column adds limited independent analytical structure beyond the categorisation.
